statement: Research I labels every claim with one of five evidence grades: FACT, DOCUMENTED BEHAVIOR, EMPIRICAL, INFERENCE, SPECULATION; downstream consumers must carry the grade with the claim.
Claims labelled SPECULATION are hypotheses to test and must never be treated as findings.
research_needed: Each SPECULATION-labelled claim reused by Entrybound needs its own test.

statement: Where evidence was sought and not found the text says unverified; per the project's standing instruction unresolved uncertainty is preserved rather than filled in.
Thirteen research passes ran against primary sources; a fourteenth fact-checked only the fifteen highest-stakes or contradictory claims, so the remaining claims were not re-verified by that pass.
research_needed: Re-verification of any non-fact-checked claim that Entrybound decisions depend on.

statement: Stack Overflow was unreachable (HTTP 403); the recurring-developer-confusion argument rests on issue trackers and mailing lists, strong for multi-year recurrence but weak for breadth of audience.
research_needed: Independent measurement of audience breadth for archive pain (Q&A view counts, surveys).

statement: Adoption metrics are not comparable across registries (weekly, rolling, cumulative, all-time, dependent counts, importers); no cross-ecosystem leaderboard may be built from the §5 tables — doing so is a category error.
Some 2026-dated CVEs lacked published MITRE records and were confirmed via GitHub Security Advisories or OSV instead; these are marked in-text.
research_needed: Re-check marked 2026 CVEs against MITRE/NVD once published.

statement: The internal design of Alpine's apk v3 package format could not be sourced from a primary source.
research_needed: Primary-source analysis of apk v3/ADB format if it becomes an adapter candidate.

statement: Per-implementation behavior for a hardlink appearing before its target could not be sourced.
research_needed: Differential test of tar implementations on hardlink-before-target archives.
decision_needed: How should Entrybound's tar import adapter treat a hardlink preceding its target?

statement: No published breakdown was found of what fraction of reproducible-build failures originate in the archive layer.
research_needed: Analysis of reproducible-builds issue databases (e.g. Debian notes) to attribute failures to archive tooling.

refines_or_supersedes: corrects earlier R1 research passes (internal §0.3 correction)
research_needed: Confirm the Node release that introduced the core ZIP API.

refines_or_supersedes: corrects earlier R1 research passes (internal §0.3 correction)

refines_or_supersedes: corrects earlier R1 research passes (internal §0.3 correction)

refines_or_supersedes: corrects earlier R1 research passes (internal §0.3 correction)
research_needed: Track whether zlib-rs becomes flate2's default backend.

statement: apk-tools 3.x shipped in Alpine 3.23.0 (2025-12-03) retaining v2 index/package compatibility; the tar-abandoning ADB format is not Alpine's default and its design is unverified.
refines_or_supersedes: corrects earlier R1 research passes (internal §0.3 correction)
research_needed: Primary source on ADB format design.

statement: Research I verdict is GO WITH REVISED SCOPE: the briefed thesis is falsified in three of four load-bearing parts and confirmed in one (determinism).
decision_needed: Does the current Entrybound scope still conform to the Research I revised scope, or have later gates superseded it?

statement: Safe-by-default extraction should not be the headline: runtimes are absorbing it (Python 3.14 data filter default, Go os.Root, .NET 7 TarFile escape checks, Node core ZIP), so entering on safety is entering a shrinking market.
evidence_in_source: FACT for runtime changes; INFERENCE for market conclusion
research_needed: Evidence on whether developers still face unsafe extraction on current runtimes (runtime version distribution in the field).
decision_needed: Is safety a supporting property rather than Entrybound's headline?

statement: Runtime absorption facts: Python 3.14 tarfile data filter default; Go 1.24 os.Root and 1.25 metadata methods; .NET TarFile.ExtractToDirectory throws on name and symlink escape since .NET 7; Node v26.8.0 core ZIP API.

A unified multi-format facade over tar, ZIP and 7z is falsified: it necessarily degenerates into a capability-query API where callers branch on format anyway (Commons Compress streaming ZIP warning, yauzl streaming refusal, mholt/archives callback).
research_needed: API usability study of any multi-format import surface Entrybound exposes.
decision_needed: Do Entrybound's legacy import adapters expose format-specific capability differences explicitly rather than a lowest-common-denominator facade?

statement: Apache Commons Compress warns its streaming ZIP reader may return false contents; mholt/archives hands each entry to a caller callback, leaving the extraction-safety decision with the caller.

Three languages in six months is falsified: native distribution cost (zstd-jni 18 platform triples), semantic drift (CVE-2025-62518 in four forks of one codebase), and slow default changes (a Python PEP over three releases) make it infeasible.
If four forks of one codebase drift, three independent implementations advertising identical semantics will drift worse, and the advertisement makes the drift dangerous.
research_needed: Differential testing between Entrybound's reference implementation and any independent reader to measure semantic drift.
decision_needed: How will Entrybound guard an independent reader against semantic drift from the reference?

statement: Determinism is a real unclaimed gap: no archiver appears in the Reproducible Builds SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH tool table (~25 tools), and its reference document concedes post-processing when tools lack reproducible options.
research_needed: Re-check the RB tool table for archivers at decision time.

statement: Eight independent determinism workarounds exist: Debian strip-nondeterminism, Fedora add-determinism, wheel 1980 floor with SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH, pacote fixed 1985 mtime, Bazel pkg_tar portable_mtime, Go x/mod/zip canonical form, Nix fetchzip hashing the extracted tree, Homebrew gzip.
Docker/OCI ships tar-split, a per-layer side-car storing raw tar header bytes verbatim, because re-taring an unpacked tree does not reproduce original bytes.
evidence_in_source: FACT for behavior; INFERENCE for framing
decision_needed: Must Entrybound's legacy import retain enough raw header information to re-emit byte-identical legacy archives?

statement: Across eight ecosystems, zero libraries offer write-me-a-byte-identical-archive as an API call.
research_needed: Up-to-date survey of archive libraries for a deterministic-output API.

statement: Maintenance asymmetry: tar libraries are actively released (tar-stream, flate2, node-tar) while high-adoption ZIP/xz libraries are stale — jszip since 2022-08-02, extract-zip since 2020-06-10, DotNetZip deprecated with unpatched CVE-2024-48510, xz2 since 2022-06-06.
research_needed: Re-measure staleness at decision time.
decision_needed: Does the ZIP-side wedge apply to Entrybound given it ships a native container rather than a ZIP library?

statement: The incumbent is free, pre-installed and invisible to measurement; in Go, archive/tar (28,261 public importers) beats mholt/archives (228) by about two orders of magnitude; a successor must beat zero dependencies.
decision_needed: What will make adopting Entrybound worth a new dependency over stdlib archive modules?

statement: Roughly 250 billion archive extractions per week occur across npm and PyPI alone, derived from registry download totals, almost none visible in third-party library counts.
evidence_in_source: FACT derived from registry totals (assumes downloads equal extractions)
research_needed: Validate the download-to-extraction equivalence; CI/mirror inflation is acknowledged in §5.4.

statement: Lead with determinism: ship a declared canonical profile and a byte-identity guarantee scoped to a pinned tuple of format, metadata policy, codec and codec parameters.
research_needed: Cross-platform, cross-version reproducibility experiments for each pinned tuple.
decision_needed: What exactly is in Entrybound's pinned determinism tuple (planner version, codec versions, thread count)?

statement: Provide a content hash over a canonical manifest that is stable across all pinned tuples (format, metadata policy, codec, parameters), on the Go dirhash model.
research_needed: Verify that logical identity is invariant under codec/profile changes.
decision_needed: Which Entrybound identity root (e.g. LAI/PCR) plays the role of the tuple-independent manifest hash?

statement: Emit conformant tar and ZIP; do not invent a format. New formats (PNA 18 stars, Jubako/arx 164) failed to displace anything, while backward-compatible retrofits (eStargz, zstd:chunked) succeeded.
research_needed: Adoption evidence for native-format archivers versus compatible retrofits.
decision_needed: Entrybound ships a native container (ECF); which later authority overrides this recommendation, and does conformant tar/ZIP export remain a v1 requirement?

statement: Build extraction on kernel containment, not path validation; every §7 bypass is a disagreement between a string validator and the filesystem, and path-prefix checking is a defect class.
evidence_in_source: INFERENCE from Docker, Go os.Root precedent
research_needed: Platform feasibility of handle-relative extraction on Linux, macOS and Windows in safe Rust.

statement: One language first: Rust, chosen for containment primitives, codec ecosystem, and because the Rust archive stack has the worst maintenance profile surveyed (four tar RUSTSEC advisories, zip crate seven breaking majors in fifteen months, async crates held as forks).
evidence_in_source: FACT for ecosystem data; INFERENCE for choice

statement: Treat the conformance suite as a first-class, possibly primary deliverable: the ~48 §8 behaviors have no executable arbiter; a public differential test corpus is valuable even if the library fails.
decision_needed: Is the conformance corpus published as a standalone deliverable independent of the library?

statement: Find the distribution wedge before writing the second thousand lines: every adjacent displacement (ripgrep in VS Code, zlib-ng/zlib-rs behind an ABI, uv behind pip commands, eStargz in BuildKit) arrived inside something already installed.
research_needed: Gatekeeper/host-tool analysis of candidate embedding channels.
decision_needed: What installed host will carry Entrybound to users?

statement: Scores: inherited market 9/10, pain recurrence 9/10, fragmentation 8/10, successor gap 7/10; migration feasibility 4/10, multilingual feasibility 3/10, six-month v1 feasibility 3/10, category recognition 4/10 (reasoning in §18).
evidence_in_source: author judgement; reasoning in §18 outside this slice
research_needed: Cross-check against §18 and later opportunity research.

statement: Every mature archive library separates a container (ordered entries with metadata) from a codec (byte-stream compressor): libarchive format vs filter families, Commons Compress archivers vs compressors, Rust tar excluding compression, Go archive/tar silent on compression.
Most category API confusion comes from fusing container and codec at the surface, e.g. shutil.make_archive treating zip/gztar/zstdtar as one parameter despite very different access properties.
research_needed: Usability evidence that separate container/codec choices reduce misuse.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound's API/CLI expose layout/access properties separately from compression profile?

statement: Preserve the familiar archive mental model: the tar verb set (create, extract, list, append, update) is inherited and load-bearing across five decades and every major language (node-tar reproduces c/x/t/r/u).
research_needed: CLI usability testing with tar/zip-literate users.
decision_needed: Which traditional verbs (append/update in particular) does Entrybound's CLI keep?

statement: Core conceptual surface a successor must cover: Create (sink, container+codec, entries from paths/buffers/streams), Inspect (enumerate metadata without reading data), Extract (materialize entries subject to policy).
Conceptual surface includes Stream (all operations against non-seekable source or sink) and Random access (read entry N without reading entries 1..N-1).
Metadata surface: mode, uid/gid, uname/gname, mtime and possibly atime/ctime/birthtime, link targets, device numbers, xattrs, ACLs.
decision_needed: Which of these metadata classes are v1 critical vs optional in Entrybound namespaces?

statement: Policy surface: overwrite semantics, filtering, path rewriting and safety constraints.
Failure surface: distinguish corrupt from unsupported from I/O errors, and decide what is left on disk after failure.
Observation surface: progress and cancellation.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound's library API offer first-class progress and cancellation?

statement: Determinism surface: byte-identical output for identical logical input.
research_needed: Reproducibility test matrix.

statement: Weak points across the category: failure taxonomies are conflated almost everywhere; progress/cancellation are absent from every stdlib surveyed and first-class in exactly two libraries; determinism is a bolt-on everywhere.
Streaming versus seekable operation is the load-bearing axis and the first thing a successor must model explicitly rather than hide.
decision_needed: How does Entrybound surface STREAM vs INDEXED access requirements in API types?

statement: Libraries encode seekability explicitly: Python tarfile 'filemode|' stream mode; Go zip.NewReader needs io.ReaderAt plus size while NewWriter does not; Commons Compress says always prefer ZipFile; SharpCompress splits forward-only Readers from random-access Archives (cleanest articulation).

ZIP's authority is the central directory at end of file (local headers redundant, not to be trusted); tar has no index and ends with two zero records. ZIP gets random access and per-entry codecs but needs a seek; tar streams one-pass but every listing is a full scan.
A compression codec transforms byte streams only: gzip members concatenate with no name table, index or directory (RFC 1952); DEFLATE does not attempt random access (RFC 1951).

Packaging artifacts are a container plus naming convention, content-hash manifest and overlay/deletion semantics: wheel RECORD requires sha256+ (md5/sha1 forbidden), .deb is ar with fixed member order, OCI layer is tar with media types and .wh. whiteouts.
decision_needed: Should OCI whiteouts/wheel RECORD semantics be modelled by legacy adapters?

statement: Every packaging ecosystem reuses the archive layer unchanged and writes its own wrapper for manifest and overlay semantics.
Filesystem images (SquashFS, DwarFS, EROFS) have directory indexes and block deduplication and leave the archive category once randomly addressable by path at OS level.
decision_needed: Is OS-level mounting (FUSE/ProjFS) out of Entrybound scope?

statement: Backup systems (restic, borg, kopia) abandon the sequential container: content-defined chunking with a separate index turns extract-entry-N into a graph traversal, which R1 names as the boundary marker of the archive category.
research_needed: Measure whether CDC plus index materially harms single-entry extraction cost and streaming in Entrybound.
decision_needed: Entrybound uses CDC and dedup; how is it reconciled with R1 placing CDC-plus-index outside the archive category?

statement: A successor serving packaging, imaging and backup from one abstraction will fail because they need different data structures; the archive category proper is interchange: bytes readable by a tool the author does not control.
decision_needed: Is Entrybound scoped as interchange, and which packaging/backup features are explicitly excluded?

statement: V7 tar (1979): 512-byte records; header name(100) mode uid gid size mtime checksum linkflag linkname(100); end-of-archive is two zero records; file name length limited to 100 characters.
evidence_in_source: FACT (Library of Congress, V7 man page)

statement: ustar (POSIX.1-1988) adds a 155-byte prefix allowing 255-byte paths only if splittable at '/'; symlink targets stay capped at 100 bytes; octal fields cap size at 8 GiB and uid/gid/device at 2^21.
decision_needed: When exporting to tar, which dialect does Entrybound use for names/targets/sizes exceeding ustar limits?

statement: GNU tar extensions: L/K pseudo-entries for long names and link names, sparse files, incremental archives (self-described as incompatible with other formats), and base-256 numeric encoding (high bit set, two's complement, up to 95-bit values).

pax (POSIX.1-2001) extended headers carry length-prefixed key=value records (path, linkpath, size, mtime, atime, uid, gid, uname, gname, charset, comment) that override the following ustar header fields; vendor keyspaces SCHILY.*, GNU.sparse.*, LIBARCHIVE.* followed.
A modern tar reader must implement four header dialects (v7, ustar, GNU, pax) and at least three numeric encodings (octal, base-256, pax decimal) to read archives in circulation.
research_needed: Corpus coverage test of Entrybound tar import across dialects.

statement: First APPNOTE.TXT dated 1990-03-15 (Library of Congress); the commonly cited PKWARE 1989 date refers to PKZIP release and is unverified from a primary source.
research_needed: Primary source for PKZIP 1989 release (low importance).

statement: APPNOTE accretion: 4.5 (2001) ZIP64 >65535 entries and >4 GB; 4.6 bzip2; 5.1 AES; 6.2 central-directory encryption; 6.3.0 (2006) UTF-8 filename bit 11; 6.3.7 zstd; 6.3.8 zstd method-ID conflict resolution; current 6.3.10 (2022-11-01).
decision_needed: Which APPNOTE version does Entrybound's ZIP import/export target?

statement: Sixteen years elapsed between ZIP shipping and acquiring a way to declare a filename as UTF-8 (bit 11, APPNOTE 6.3.0, 2006).
zstd in ZIP received two method IDs (20 and 93); Python zipfile reads both but writes only 93, illustrating compatibility physics of registry conflicts.
research_needed: Test which ZIP readers accept method 93 vs 20.
decision_needed: Which zstd method IDs does Entrybound's ZIP import accept and export write?

statement: Info-ZIP contributed Unicode Path extra field 0x7075; its releases stalled (Zip 3.0 2008, UnZip 6.0 2009, betas stuck at 2015); Debian ships unzip 6.0-31 and zip 3.0-16; FreeBSD replaced Info-ZIP with a libarchive-based compatible unzip.
gzip (0.1 in 1992, 1.0 in 1993) was created to replace compress over LZW patent concerns; DEFLATE and gzip were formalized as RFC 1951/1952 in May 1996 stressing patent-free implementability.
bzip2 uses Burrows-Wheeler plus Huffman with 100k-900k blocks (FACT); Julian Seward's 1996 first release is unverified against a primary source.
research_needed: Primary source for bzip2 first release date (low importance).

statement: 7-Zip 2.00 released 1999-07-18; 7z format arrived in 2.30 beta (2001-08-30); xz spec 1.0.0 released January 2009 (secondary source); xz's Index exists to reach the start of any Block for random access.
evidence_in_source: FACT (7-Zip history, xz spec); xz date secondary

statement: xz is the first mainstream codec to admit that seekability matters, via its block Index.

zstd adoption is the fastest documented: Meta 2016 (~3-5x zlib speed), RFC 8478 then RFC 8878 (2021); Arch 2019 (~0.8% larger, ~1300% faster decompression); Fedora F31 RPM; dpkg 1.21.18; OCI tar+zstd; ZIP method 93; Python 3.14; .NET 11 ZstandardStream approved; Node v23.8.0.
zstd is the only format surveyed with a real IETF specification and multiple independent implementations, which makes a pure-Rust decoder (ruzstd, 61M downloads) viable.
research_needed: Conformance/performance evaluation of pure-Rust zstd decoders against libzstd.
decision_needed: Can Entrybound's independent reader or decoder longevity story rely on a pure-Rust zstd decoder?

statement: CVE-2024-3094 (xz-utils 5.6.0/5.6.1, CVSS 10.0): an onboarded maintainer hid an sshd backdoor via build-to-host.m4 present only in release tarballs, not git, with payload in binary test files.

In CVE-2024-3094 no archive was malformed and no parser misbehaved, so parser hardening would not have helped; the vector broke the assumption that reviewing a repository equals reviewing its release artifact.
research_needed: Evaluate reproducible release-artifact generation and source-to-artifact binding for Entrybound releases and dependencies.
decision_needed: How will Entrybound bind its own release artifacts to reviewed source and vet codec dependencies?

statement: tar has no index: the format is a record stream terminated by two zero blocks, with nowhere for an index without breaking append-by-concatenation; every listing is a scan.
.tar.gz has no random access at all: DEFLATE does not support it, so a tar offset index is useless without a codec-level index (as xz Index and zstd seekable format re-add).
Solid compression trades random access for ratio; Commons Compress notes 7z random access under solid compression is likely significantly slower than sequential access.
research_needed: Measure random-access latency versus ratio for Entrybound chunk grouping/lookback settings.
decision_needed: What bound does Entrybound place on solid-group size to preserve random access?

statement: ZIP data descriptors (APPNOTE 4.4.4 bit 3) are unavoidable when output is non-seekable, because a size not yet known cannot be written into an already-emitted header.
tar requires entry size before the header (Go ErrWriteTooLong); a tar entry from a stream of unknown length requires buffering to memory or a temp file; tar has no data-descriptor equivalent.
research_needed: Measure staging cost of streaming tar export of unknown-length entries.
decision_needed: How does Entrybound's tar export stage unknown-length inputs (memory vs temp file bounds)?

statement: tar octal numeric fields (a 1979 tape-readability choice) force every reader to handle octal, GNU base-256 and pax size= overrides.
tar's 100-byte name field and 155-byte prefix split are historical accidents preserved for compatibility.
ZIP MS-DOS timestamps use 1980-relative years, 2-second precision and no timezone; Python interprets central-directory timestamps as local time to match other tools.
decision_needed: How does Entrybound's ZIP import reconcile DOS local time with UTC extended timestamps?

statement: ZIP filename encoding is ambiguous: raw bytes, general purpose bit 11 and Info-ZIP 0x7075 overlap, with no specified default when bit 11 is unset; the CP437 assumption is convention, not specification.
research_needed: Survey of real-world non-UTF-8 ZIP names and tool interpretations.
decision_needed: What encoding does Entrybound's ZIP import assume for bit-11-unset names, and how are raw bytes preserved?

statement: ZIP central-directory/local-header duplication, originally for multi-disk recovery and in-place append, is now the largest parser-disagreement surface in the category.
tar entry ordering is undefined; GNU tar's default order is whatever the operating system returns.
Historical format accidents are fixable only by a new format, which will not be adopted.
research_needed: Adoption evidence for new archive formats that coexist with legacy export.
decision_needed: Entrybound defines a native container; what adoption strategy counters R1's prediction that a new format will not be adopted?

statement: The tarbomb (flat top-level extraction) is a fixable tooling defect: nothing in tar forbids it and GNU tar's --one-top-level is opt-in.
decision_needed: Should Entrybound extraction default to a single top-level directory or warn on flat archives?

statement: Fully-trusted extraction as a default is an avoidable library mistake; Python, node-tar, bsdtar and Rust tar converged independently on the same fix.
Streaming readers must not share an interface shape indistinguishable from correct (seekable) readers; the ZIP format makes streaming reads lossy and callers select them by accident.
evidence_in_source: INFERENCE grounded in Commons Compress warning
research_needed: API usability testing of STREAM vs INDEXED readers.

statement: Facade APIs must not hide the seekability decision at the moment the developer is choosing it.
Essential properties and historical accidents are the compatibility bill any successor inherits; library design mistakes are the entire opportunity.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound's native container change which accidents it inherits (only on legacy import/export paths)?

statement: In every ecosystem the dominant implementation is the standard library or one mature C library; churn, abandonment and CVEs concentrate in the third-party layer above them.

CVE-2007-4559 (tarfile unsanitized member names) carried only a documentation warning for fifteen years until Trellix's 2022 re-disclosure estimated hundreds of thousands of vulnerable repositories; PEP 706 then added filter= with three named policies.
Design principle to adopt verbatim (PEP 706, Viktorin): documentation warnings are not enough; whenever possible an unsafe operation should be explicitly requested.
decision_needed: Which Entrybound extraction behaviours require explicit opt-in flags?

statement: Python's data filter (default since 3.14) refuses absolute and out-of-destination paths, normalizes and validates link targets, refuses device files and FIFOs, clears setuid/setgid/sticky, and discards uid/gid.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound's default extraction policy meet or exceed the data filter baseline?

statement: After shipping, Python's filters took five CVEs (gh-135034) rooted in unnormalized link targets and realpath behavior; CVE-2026-3644 was bypassed three more times; CVE-2026-11940 recreated a hardlink to a deeper symlink at a shallower path.
Extraction policy must apply on every code path: gh-151987 found TarFile.extract() skipping the filter entirely on its hardlink-fallback path.
research_needed: Code-path coverage tests showing confinement applies on all fallback paths.

statement: A pre-extraction metadata check cannot model ordering, link resolution and OS path semantics that determine filesystem effects; every tarfile filter bypass was a gap between what the header says and what the filesystem does.
evidence_in_source: INFERENCE (called the single most important technical lesson)

statement: Python concedes no filter blocks all dangers; residue includes denial of service, filename confusables, case-insensitive shadowing and live-data tampering during extraction — a successor's threat model must address or explicitly state these.
research_needed: Tests for confusable and case-folding collisions on NTFS/APFS.
decision_needed: Which residual extraction threats does Entrybound handle versus declare out of scope?

statement: Python zipfile silently mangles names: strips leading slashes and drive letters, removes all '..' components, and replaces Windows-illegal characters with '_'; PEP 706 filters were never extended to ZIP and shutil.unpack_archive rejects filter for zip.
Extraction must not silently relocate entries: with zipfile a member '../evil' lands as 'evil' with no error, so callers cannot distinguish faithful extraction from relocation.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound report every path rewrite in its FidelityReport or refuse instead?

statement: zipfile.extractall has never restored Unix modes from external_attr (bpo-15795, filed 2012, still open); a 2026 re-report frames it as confidentiality regression since a 0o600 file extracts world-readable.
Permission handling on extraction must not widen access relative to the archived mode; losing restrictive modes (0o600 becoming world-readable) is a confidentiality defect.
research_needed: Cross-platform test of restrictive-mode restoration.

statement: Python 3.14: data filter default, compression.zstd (PEP 784), ZIP_ZSTANDARD, SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH honored in ZipFile.writestr(), and gzip.compress() defaulting to mtime=0 for reproducible output.
Windows Explorer emits Deflate64 for ZIP archives over 2 GB; zipfile lacks Deflate64 and AES, so zipfile-deflate64 monkey-patches zipfile, and stream-unzip exists for non-seekable input.
research_needed: Corpus of Explorer-produced large ZIPs to test Deflate64 decode.
decision_needed: Must Entrybound's ZIP import decode Deflate64 (and ZIP AES) for v1?

statement: py7zr exists because stdlib lacks 7z, needs 300-700 MiB free RAM and recommends subprocess for speed; it re-encountered stdlib defect classes: CVE-2022-44900 traversal, CVE-2026-23879 symlink-chain write, CVE-2026-55195 decompression bomb. ratarmount exists because tar lacks random access.

Go archive/tar is strictly sequential, archive/zip needs io.ReaderAt plus size, and neither ships ExtractAll; Go's Header (AccessTime, ChangeTime, PAXRecords, explicit Format) is the best metadata model surveyed.
Go FileInfoHeader uses only the base filename and cannot infer a symlink target, the most common cause of flattened tarballs and symlinks silently becoming empty regular files.
decision_needed: Does Entrybound's pack path capture link targets and relative paths explicitly with a diagnostic on failure?

statement: Go ErrInsecurePath shipped in 1.20 only behind GODEBUG tarinsecurepath=0, still not default as of Go 1.27; safe-by-default proposal #57850 is on Hold because Docker images frequently include absolute paths.
research_needed: Measure frequency of absolute paths in real container-layer tarballs.
decision_needed: How does Entrybound's tar import represent absolute-path entries from Docker layers (strip, contain, reject)?

statement: Go issue #33036 requesting an API for resource limits against zip bombs has been open since 2019-07-10 with no milestone.

Go 1.24 os.Root and 1.25's full metadata method set (Chmod, Chown, Chtimes, Lchown, Link, MkdirAll, Readlink, RemoveAll, Rename, Symlink, WriteFile...) provide kernel containment; Neil names archive extraction as the motivating case for why path validation fails.
As of Go 1.25 a correct extractor is roughly sixty lines on top of os.Root, yet the standard library does not ship one.
research_needed: Implement to confirm (low priority).

statement: mholt/archives (successor to mholt/archiver, archived Nov 2024) has the cleanest unified API found: Format/Archiver/Extractor/Compressor, context.Context on every top-level call, io/fs views, header sniffing; it never writes to disk and is silent on determinism.
hashicorp/go-extract is the only surveyed library shipping numeric extraction defaults: 1 GB max extraction size, 100,000 max files, 60 s max time, 1 GB max input.
research_needed: Measure legitimate-archive distributions to calibrate default budgets.
decision_needed: What default budget values does Entrybound choose, and on what evidence?

statement: Docker's chrootarchive documents that sanitizing symlinks by string inspection is inherently racy, citing CVE-2018-15664.

Rust has the best codec layer: flate2 (643M downloads, 6,393 reverse deps) defaults to pure-Rust with zlib-rs fastest; bzip2 0.6.0 defaulted to libbz2-rs-sys (9-15% faster compression, MIRI-verified unsafe, independent audit); zlib-rs >30M downloads, not yet flate2 default.
decision_needed: Which codec backends (pure-Rust vs C) does Entrybound's dependency policy require?

statement: The Rust tar crate moved to composefs/tar-rs after ~18 months of lapsed releases; it has four RUSTSEC advisories including RUSTSEC-2026-0067 (unpack_in chmods through symlinks via fs::metadata) and RUSTSEC-2026-0068 (PAX size ignored when ustar size nonzero).
decision_needed: Does Entrybound depend on the tar crate for legacy import/export, and with what vetting?

statement: Metadata operations during extraction must not follow symlinks (RUSTSEC-2026-0067 used following fs::metadata and chmodded arbitrary directories).

tar readers must apply PAX size overrides consistently; ignoring PAX size when the ustar size is nonzero (RUSTSEC-2026-0068) is the same entry-smuggling class as CVE-2025-62518, reaching the sync crate five months later.
research_needed: Differential corpus cases for PAX/ustar size desync.

statement: The zip crate had seven breaking majors in ~15 months with dependents pinned across ^0.6, ^2, ~2.5.0, ^2.6; RUSTSEC-2025-0168/CVE-2025-29787 (CVSS 7.3) is symlink escape in ZipArchive::extract despite correct enclosed_name(), because the final canonicalized path was never checked.

statement: A ZIP file cannot be interpreted start-to-finish from a stream without sacrificing correctness; local file headers are denounced by the spec as unreliable, so any streaming unzip library is either dishonest or nonconformant (yauzl).

statement: tar pads all file data to 512-byte multiples, so a 100-byte file costs at least 1,024 bytes before compression (small-entry amplification).

statement: Extracting one file from a large .tar.gz is O(whole archive), since GzipFile restarts decompression on every seek; indexed_gzip, zindex, zran-style indexes and ratarmount exist solely because of this.

Python conflates corrupt, unsupported and I/O errors by definition (tarfile ReadError, CompressionError); zipfile has a single BadZipFile, and CRC checks are opt-in via testzip(), which returns only the first bad file's name.
Error taxonomy separating format, algorithm and checksum failures is demonstrably fixable: Go archive/zip has ErrFormat, ErrAlgorithm, ErrChecksum and node-tar a typed severity model.
Partial output on failure is universal and documented as the caller's problem: Python says clean up yourself (extract to temp), .NET says partially extracted, Rust tar does not document it at all.
No mainstream library was found offering atomic extract-to-temp-plus-rename as a built-in; whether one exists is unverified.

statement: ZIP CRC-32 lives in the central directory or a trailing data descriptor, so a streaming extractor writes every byte before it can verify; tar's header checksum covers only the header, leaving entry data entirely unverified.

statement: A safe library nobody imports fixes nothing: google/safearchive is stdlib API-compatible, yet its hardening is disabled by default for backward compatibility, it took CVE-2024-10389, and its adoption is negligible.

Case for memory safety: libarchive release notes are dominated by heap overflows, OOB, double-free and integer overflows; Chromium reports ~70% of serious bugs are memory-safety; OSS-Fuzz's 15% libarchive coverage shows 'it is fuzzed' is not evidence, and coverage is usually unpublished.

Every Rust archive advisory found is a logic bug, not a memory bug: RUSTSEC-2018-0002, -2021-0080, -2026-0067, -2026-0068 (tar), -2025-0168 (zip), -2025-0110/0111 (async forks) — traversal, symlink escape, chmod outside root, PAX/ustar desync.

Rust reimplementations reintroduced hazards the C incumbent had solved at the API level (RUSTSEC-2025-0168 lacked the final-path check libarchive's SECURE_SYMLINKS provided); the largest realized loss, CVE-2024-3094, was supply chain no rewrite would touch.
libzip's roughly nine-year clean CVE record shows a well-scoped C library can hold up.
